If the implementer reports a well-formed sha it never created, the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`` is false: `three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js:238-242` says the reported sha "is not itself detected: if the branch has commits, a phase whose implementer reported a sha it never created still reviews the real diff and closes on it. Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository, which this script cannot do — it has no shell." three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — `Each gets the diff, the plan, and the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest` contradicts the shipped skill and the script. `three-loop-workflow/SKILL.md:62`: "Reviewers are fresh subagents receiving the diff and the plan — and **nothing else**". `three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js:328-332`: "The diff and the plan, and nothing else. three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:147 — `3. Record the surviving hypothesis and check it with `scripts/verify-plan.sh` before you edit anything.` names a script that does not exist. `find . -name 'verify-plan*'` returns nothing; the only shell scripts in the tree are `scripts/accept-release.sh`, `scripts/negative-test.sh`, `three-loop-workflow/scripts/check-workflow-syntax.sh`. three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:218 — The rewritten Workflow-mode note states the opposite of what the script does. It claims "the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`". `phase.js` cannot do this and says so: lines 237-243 read "a fabricated sha does not survive into the returned `headSha`, but it is not itself detected: if the branch has commits, a phase whose implementer reported a sha it never created still reviews the real diff and closes on it. Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository" — a Workflow script has no shell. `scripts/sim-phase.js:290` asserts only that a fabricated sha cannot close a phase **on an empty diff**, which is the weaker property the deleted sentence described. CLAUDE.md:144-146 states the same limit. Worse, this is a regression of a finding the previous release already fixed: docs/measurements/2026-07-30-round-data/harden-audit-findings-plan.md:180 records "`phase.js` and `build.md` both claimed the fabricated-sha hole was closed. It is not". The change also violates plan Decision D2, which chose option (b) — restate the note *against `phase.js`* — precisely because "deleting it loses the only place that limit is written down". The commit deletes the limit and replaces it with a false capability claim, so a reader now believes a hole is closed that is open.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — "Each gets the diff, the plan, and the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest" contradicts the shipped script and the sentence it sits in. `phase.js:328-332`: "The diff and the plan, and nothing else. Not the implementer's summary, not its list of low-confidence areas, not an instruction about where to look: the value of a second reviewer is that it never saw the reasoning that produced the change, and a shared attention directive correlates the two readings it is there to keep independent. The concerns are returned to the caller instead". The `concerns` field (phase.js:135, 259, 426) is returned to the caller, never sent to a reviewer. The rest of the same line still asserts "the value comes from their independence", which the added clause defeats. The plan's Goal item was "state exactly what each reviewer receives"; the text states the opposite of what is sent, and changing what reviewers receive is a rule stated elsewhere in the skill, which the plan's Non-goals exclude (plan.md:24). The review prompt block at build.md:47-58 was left unchanged, so the document now instructs two mutually exclusive things.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — "Fix every reported blocking finding, then triage: while the diff is still moving, confirming each claim first costs a round you will spend anyway" inverts the skill's central triage rule. It contradicts the section immediately above it — build.md:70 "**Do not fix a finding you have not confirmed.**" and build.md:76 "**The confirmed count is what closes the phase**, not the reported one. Skipping triage means a phantom finding consumes a fix round and can exhaust the round cap on code that was already correct" — and it contradicts SKILL.md:71, phase.js:369-393 ("Triage before counting … Closing on the RAW count lets a phantom defect consume a fix round and exhaust the cap on already-correct code"), and CLAUDE.md's "triage findings before counting them". The stated rationale is also backwards: fixing unconfirmed findings is what spends rounds on non-defects. Plan Goal item was "make the ordering of the Fix and Triage steps explicit"; the document's actual order is Triage then Fix, so this makes the ordering explicitly wrong. Non-goal violation (plan.md:24).

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:147 — "Record the surviving hypothesis and check it with `scripts/verify-plan.sh` before you edit anything" points at a script that does not exist. `scripts/` contains only `accept-release.sh`, `negative-test.sh`, `sim-phase.js`, `sim-scenarios.js`; a repo-wide search for `verify-plan` returns nothing outside this new line. This is the exact failure CLAUDE.md's Engineering Norms name: "Do not claim a script does something without testing that it does." It is also a skill-internal path pointing into the *host repo's* `scripts/`, which is not a path the skill can assume exists in any consuming project. The plan's Goal asked for "a concrete recording step" for Diagnosis; a step that cannot be executed is not one, and a plan-verification script is not a hypothesis-recording step either.

reported: **`scripts/accept-release.sh:155-156` — the new word-numeral arm has no word boundaries, so the gate fails on ordinary prose.** `WORDNUM` is an unanchored alternation, so `one` matches inside `done`, `none`, `someone`, `everyone`, `money`, `unioned`. Combined with `[^.]{0,40}…findings` and the new `-i` flag, any of those within 40 non-period characters before the word `findings` trips the sweep. Demonstrated against the real check: appending the sentence `None of the blocking findings survived triage this round.` to `three-loop-workflow/references/build.md` produces `FAIL a statistic is back in the shipped skill: three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:224` and a non-zero exit. Same for `Once the reviewer is done, triage the reported findings.`, `It is done; the confirmed findings close the phase.`, `unioned … findings`. These are not contrived — `none of the blocking findings` and `unioned findings` are the exact register of this skill's triage prose, and `plan.md:79` already uses `unioned` in a sentence about findings (it only escapes because the word falls *after* `findings`). This is a CI-blocking gate on the load-bearing `scripts/**` surface that fires on correct documents, which the file's own header (`accept-release.sh:20-21`) calls out as "worse than useless — it accuses correct documents of being stale". `\b` around the numeral group fixes it.

**`scripts/accept-release.sh:147-159` and `:362-378` land squarely in the plan's Non-goals.** `plan.md:23` reads "**`build.md` only.** No change to `SKILL.md`, to `phase.js`, or to any other file." Two commits change `scripts/accept-release.sh` (`d3d7d51` +18, `5e4b783` +14), and at 32 of the 37 added lines the out-of-scope file is the *majority* of the diff. `d3d7d51`'s message argues the deviation explicitly ("Outside plan.md:24's 'build.md only', and stated as such"); `5e4b783` does not mention scope at all. `build.md:21` — a rule in the file being edited — says "If the plan conflicts with what you find in the code, stop and say so… go fix the plan", and the plan was never amended: `.agent/revise-build-md/` still contains only the original `plan.md`. Either amend the Non-goal with a recorded Decision or split the gate work out. The caller may well accept the deviation on its merits; it should not be accepted silently.

scripts/accept-release.sh:147-156 and :362-379 — the entire gate change lands in the plan's Non-goals. plan.md:23 reads "**`build.md` only.** No change to `SKILL.md`, to `phase.js`, or to any other file." Two separate blocks were added to a file the plan never scoped, and `scripts/**` is load-bearing under CLAUDE.md's _load-bearing-docs_, so this is Deep work with no Decision covering it (the plan records only D1 and D2, both about build.md prose). Commit d3d7d51 states the deviation in its message ("Outside plan.md:24's 'build.md only', and stated as such" — and miscites the line; the clause is plan.md:23, while plan.md:24 is the separate rules Non-goal), but build.md:21 requires the opposite response: "If the plan conflicts with what you find in the code, stop and say so. Do not decide unilaterally and do not paper over it — go fix the plan." The plan file was never amended; it still reads as a build.md-only change.

scripts/accept-release.sh:147,156 — the extended statistic sweep still passes the digit spelling of the exact figure it was added to catch. Verified by running the assembled `$STAT` from the script: `Ten of the twenty-one confirmed findings in the last release` → CAUGHT; `10 of the 21 confirmed findings in the last release` → escapes; `21 confirmed findings` → escapes; `10 of 21 confirmed findings were defects in the gates` → escapes. The pre-existing arms only cover `%`, `percentage points`, and the hardcoded literal `116 findings`, so digits are unguarded except for that one frozen string. The gate now blocks the rarer spelling and admits the common one. The comment at :151-152 makes this worse rather than disclosing it — "What it does not catch, said plainly so nobody reads this as a sweep for spelled numbers: any other quantity written as a word" names only word-spelled quantities as the gap, which reads as an assurance that digits are handled. The comment's own justification for scoping (:153-154: the skill states rule values in words, "Three fix rounds per phase", "Standard: one reviewer") is precisely the argument that a digit-scoped `[0-9]+([- ][0-9]+)?[^.]{0,40}…findings` arm is the safe one to add.

scripts/accept-release.sh:155-156 — the word-numeral arm has no word boundaries and fires on ordinary prose, and the shipped skill escapes it by one character. `$WORDNUM` is bare alternation with no `\b`/`[^A-Za-z]` anchor, so it matches inside words. Verified against the assembled pattern: `none of the findings` → CAUGHT; `Someone reviewing a diff returns findings` → CAUGHT; `a milestone reached before the reviewer reports findings` → CAUGHT; `Two reviewers, union their findings` → CAUGHT. The skill's own central rule line, three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:38 `**Standard: one reviewer. Deep: two, in parallel, independent — union their findings.**`, escapes only because the span between "two" and "findings" is 41 characters against `[^.]{0,40}`. Replacing the em dash with a colon, or deleting the word "independent", makes it CAUGHT — verified both. three-loop-workflow/references/plan.md:13 sits in the same window. So an innocuous reword of a rule sentence makes the gate print "a statistic is back in the shipped skill" and exit non-zero. That is the exact failure the comment at :153-154 claims was designed out ("a check that fired on those would be turned off within a release"), and it breaks the contract this file states for itself at :20-23 — a gate that "accuses correct documents of being stale" is "worse than useless".

scripts/accept-release.sh:365-366 — the comment asserts a shipped defect that never shipped: "A named script that is not shipped is an instruction nobody can follow, and one shipped: `scripts/verify-plan.sh`, invented in build.md's Diagnosis step, passed every check in this file". `git log --all --oneline -S'verify-plan'` returns exactly two commits, 6b25b7a (introduced it) and d3d7d51 (removed it), both on this unmerged branch; `git grep -n 'verify-plan' main` returns nothing and it is on no tag. Nothing shipped — it was introduced and reverted inside one branch. This is a false factual claim placed permanently in a load-bearing file, against that file's own stated contract at :3-6 ("Evidence quoted in permanent history has to be reproducible from the history") and CLAUDE.md's Engineering Norms ("Do not claim a script does something without testing that it does"). A future maintainer reading it will believe a released version carried a dangling script reference.

**`scripts/accept-release.sh`:277 — dropping `-r` from the same invocation turns the live check into a silent no-op, and nothing notices.** `_stat_hits=$(stat_scan three-loop-workflow/ || true)` at :407: without `-r`, grep refuses a directory, writes to stderr, exits 1, `|| true` swallows it, `_stat_hits` is empty, and the script prints `ok no statistics anywhere in the shipped skill`. Demonstrated in the same clone with the same planted sentence: `grep -niHE` (only `-r` removed) gave `ok the statistic sweep behaves on 68 pinned sentences`, `ok every piece of the sweep is pinned by a case (44 mutations, each one noticed)`, `ok no statistics anywhere in the shipped skill`, `ACCEPT: all checks passed`. This is strictly worse than the `-i` case — `-i` narrows the sweep, `-r` disables it entirely — and it is the same false claim at :271: the fixture table runs `stat_scan` against a single regular file, where `-r` never decides anything, so no case can ever pin it. Same root as the finding above, different fix: pinning `-i` needs a capitalised fixture; pinning `-r` needs the live scan to assert it actually read files (or a directory-shaped fixture).
